title: Power Automate process mining: tabs and customisable layouts in the process intelligence experience
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout facts, licensing statements and record-reassignment guidance match the sources checked. It accurately distinguishes documented process-mining controls from unanswered questions about the new interface and public tabs.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The process intelligence experience is a new process-analysis interface in Power Automate Process Mining.
claims.quote: The new process intelligence experience is the next-generation interface for process analysis in Power Automate Process Mining.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The new experience replaces a single fixed overview with customisable analytical workspaces.
claims.quote: Flexibility: Create multiple tabs with different card configurations instead of a single fixed view.

claims.claim: Each process view can have its own set of analytical tabs.
claims.quote: You can have an independent set of analytical tabs per view.

claims.claim: Each tab holds its own collection of cards and visualisations.
claims.quote: Each tab maintains its own collection of cards, visualizations, and layout configuration

claims.claim: Users can arrange cards themselves.
claims.quote: Customizable layouts where you can arrange, resize, and configure cards

claims.claim: Users can resize cards themselves.
claims.quote: Customizable layouts where you can arrange, resize, and configure cards

claims.claim: Users can configure cards themselves.
claims.quote: Customizable layouts where you can arrange, resize, and configure cards

claims.quote: At the end of the tab bar, select (+). The Add tab dialog opens.

claims.quote: The Edit tabs context menu displays: ... Add tab button: + Add tab option at the bottom.

claims.claim: Tabs can be renamed.
claims.quote: Rename tab: Change the tab's name.

claims.claim: Tabs can be deleted.
claims.quote: Delete tab: Remove the tab from the dashboard.

claims.claim: Tabs can be moved to change their order.
claims.quote: Move up: Shift the tab one position to the left in the tab bar. Move down: Shift the tab one position to the right in the tab bar.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Process-mining access follows environment security and Dataverse security roles.
claims.quote: The process mining capability relies on environment security and Microsoft Dataverse security roles and privileges to grant access to its features in Power Automate.

claims.claim: Environment Maker can create processes.
claims.quote: The Environment maker role can use the process mining capabilities to create, share, and contribute to processes.

claims.claim: Environment Maker can share processes.
claims.quote: The Environment maker role can use the process mining capabilities to create, share, and contribute to processes.

claims.claim: Environment Maker can contribute to processes.
claims.quote: The Environment maker role can use the process mining capabilities to create, share, and contribute to processes.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: pilot
claims.claim: Process Mining User can only view created process reports.
claims.quote: The Process Mining User security role can only view created process reports.

claims.claim: Process Mining Application is an internal security role.
claims.quote: The Process Mining Application is an internal security role that process mining uses.

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to assign Process Mining Application to users.
claims.quote: Don't assign this security role to users.

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to modify Process Mining User privileges.
claims.quote: Don't modify the set of privileges in the Process Mining User or Process Mining Application security roles.

claims.claim: Microsoft says not to modify Process Mining Application privileges.
claims.quote: Don't modify the set of privileges in the Process Mining User or Process Mining Application security roles.

claims.claim: Conditional Access limiting Power Automate must include both Power Apps and Power Automate in Cloud apps; Power Automate alone is insufficient.
claims.quote: the following apps must be included in Cloud apps policy application: Power Apps; Power Automate. Currently, having conditional access to only Power Automate isn't enough.

claims.claim: The interface documentation describes analysis and visualisation, not autonomous actions on tenant data.
claims.quote: Searched: "process intelligence experience" "actions" "data". Opened studio-overview, tab-management and studio-dynamic-layout; these describe visualisation, filtering and layout configuration, with no autonomous tenant-data actions.

claims.claim: Disabling a process owner's account does not automatically make a co-owner the owner.
claims.quote: When a process owner's account is disabled, the co-owner of the process doesn't automatically become a new process owner.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Process mining is licensed as part of Microsoft Power Automate.
claims.quote: Process mining is licensed as part of Microsoft Power Automate.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects per-user Power Automate Premium and a tenant-wide Process Mining add-on.
claims.quote: The Power Automate Premium license is a per-user license ... The Process Mining add-on is a tenant-wide license that's available for the Power Automate Premium license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Automate Premium is a per-user licence.
claims.quote: The Power Automate Premium license is a per-user license

claims.claim: Each Power Automate Premium licence adds 50 MB of process-mining capacity.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool up to a total of 100 GB.

claims.claim: Premium process-mining capacity accumulates in a tenant-wide pool.
claims.quote: Each Power Automate Premium license adds 50 MB of process mining capacity to a tenant-wide capacity pool

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Premium capacity limit
claims.claim: Premium's capacity pool tops out at 100 GB, after which an add-on is needed to process more data.
claims.quote: up to a total of 100 GB. When you reach 100 GB, you need to purchase the Power Automate Process Mining add-on to process more data.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Process Mining add-on is tenant-wide.
claims.quote: The Process Mining add-on is a tenant-wide license that's available for the Power Automate Premium license.

claims.claim: The add-on adds another 100 GB of process-mining capacity.
claims.quote: An extra 100 GB of process mining capacity to the capacity pool, which users with the Power Automate Premium license can use.

claims.claim: The process-mining overview describes a 90-day Power Automate trial.
claims.quote: For a limited time of 90 days, the Power Automate trial license offers:

claims.claim: The overview describes a trial capacity of 100 MB per process.
claims.quote: The trial offers limited process mining capacity of 100 MB per process.

claims.claim: The licensing FAQ instead describes a free 30-day Process Mining trial.
claims.quote: Yes, Process Mining offers a free 30-day trial giving access to many of the key features of Process Mining.

claims.claim: The FAQ says the free Process Mining trial is included in the Power Automate trial.
claims.quote: The free Process Mining trial is included in the Power Automate trial.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Power BI inclusion

claims.claim: No meter specific to this experience is published at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "process intelligence experience" license pricing meter capacity public tabs preview. Opened process-advisor-overview, licensing FAQ and pay-as-you-go-meters; checked the meter inventory. No experience-specific meter found.

claims.claim: No separate price specific to the process intelligence experience is published.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No separate experience licence is published, and the tabs, layouts and experience overview pages name no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: "process intelligence experience" license pricing meter capacity public tabs preview. Opened tab-management, studio-dynamic-layout, studio-overview, process-advisor-overview and licensing FAQ. No separate experience licence found; the three interface pages name none.

claims.claim: Stored process data mostly uses Dataverse file capacity.
claims.quote: The process data we store uses mostly file capacity.

claims.claim: Importing a large amount of process data can exhaust Dataverse storage.
claims.quote: Depending on the size of the process data you import, you might run out of Dataverse storage capacity.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions: capacity
claims.claim: The documentation does not describe additional cards and tabs as consuming process-mining or Dataverse capacity.
claims.quote: Searched: "process intelligence experience" license pricing meter capacity public tabs preview. Opened studio-overview, tab-management, studio-dynamic-layout, process-advisor-overview and licensing FAQ. No card/tab capacity accounting described.

claims.claim: Process mining requires a Power Platform environment with a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: A Microsoft Power Platform environment with a Microsoft Dataverse database.

claims.claim: The required licences or trials depend on the process-mining capabilities being used.
claims.quote: The required licenses or trials depending on the capabilities you want access to.

claims.claim: Administrators can access all processes created in the environment.
claims.quote: Administrators and system customizers can access all processes created in the environment.

claims.claim: System customizers can access all processes created in the environment.
claims.quote: Administrators and system customizers can access all processes created in the environment.

claims.claim: Some default Dataverse privileges let built-in security roles use process mining without further administrator action.
claims.quote: Some privileges are set by default in Dataverse. This allows built-in security roles to use the process mining capability without further actions from system administrators.

claims.claim: The documented reassignment route is Power Platform admin center > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Reassign records.
claims.quote: Sign in to Power Platform admin center. ... Select the environment where the process is located. ... select Settings. ... Under Users + permissions, select Users. ... Select the leaving user. ... select Reassign records.

claims.claim: The receiving user needs appropriate privileges on the entities associated with the transferred records.
claims.quote: The target user should have the appropriate privileges on the different entities associated with the transferred records.

claims.claim: Environment Maker is sufficient for the receiving user for a process-mining process.
claims.quote: For process mining process, giving the Environment Maker role is sufficient.

claims.claim: The cited sharing page does not state a named administrator role required for its reassignment steps.
claims.quote: Searched: "process mining" "reassign" "administrator" "role". Opened process-mining-share in full: the reassignment section says administrator, and specifies the target user's privileges, but names no required administrator role.

claims.claim: Dataverse documents ReassignObjectsSystemUser for reassigning records owned by a specified user.
claims.quote: ReassignObjectsSystemUser Action ... Reassigns all records that are owned by a specified user to another security principal (user, team, or organization).

claims.claim: ReassignObjectsSystemUser is a general record-reassignment operation, not a process-only transfer.
claims.quote: Reassigns all records that are owned by a specified user to another security principal (user, team, or organization).

claims.claim: Changes made in Edit layout can be saved to the tab layout.
claims.quote: Save changes made in edit layout mode by selecting Save when exiting edit mode.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and .api; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No admin UI or automation control is documented to switch this experience on or off or administratively limit its tab sharing.
claims.quote: Searched: process intelligence experience admin disable sharing; process intelligence experience Power Platform API pac admin PowerShell; process mining tab sharing API Dataverse. Opened the three interface pages and security page; read pac admin and PowerShell results. No such control found.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no new data source introduced by this interface.
claims.quote: Searched: "process intelligence experience" "actions" "data"; "process intelligence experience" "Dataverse" "API". Opened studio-overview, tab-management and studio-dynamic-layout. They describe analysis of the selected process, not a new data source.
